admission.justification: A row for one of the nine in the agents' command table would present that command to every role that reads the table, so the check refuses the row. Refusing a mention would be the opposite mistake: it would fail the three guide lines that tell knowledge-convert to the user of a memory repository cloned before memory_init, so the check requires no mention and refuses none.

applicability: The nine command names of the set UNDOCUMENTED_COMMANDS, in the instruction consistency check and the CLI parser.
conditions: The check refuses no mention of them: three lines of two guide pages name knowledge-convert.
The check requires no documentation row and no mention for them.
The check refuses a row for one of them in the agents' command table.
exclusions: Every public command outside the set: the check requires one complete row in the agents' command table for it.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_role_instruction_corpus.py::test_each_public_command_requires_its_documentation_owner; mcp/tests/test_instruction_consistency.py::test_complete_instruction_documentation_and_registered_descriptions; evidence/v9/item3-dropped-assertions.md; both modules pass in the clean-copy run f3

origin.handoffEntry: MIK-R97@v9 part F item 7 (the consistency check)

statement: The nine command names of the set UNDOCUMENTED_COMMANDS are registered commands outside the agents' command table: the consistency check requires no row and no mention for them and refuses a row for one of them in that table. One of them, knowledge-convert, is told in three lines of two guide pages, for a memory repository that was cloned before memory_init.
